03f0276d-ea71-550e-87b2-3e9d039d58d4.name: Amor and Psyche – Garden
03f0276d-ea71-550e-87b2-3e9d039d58d4.description: During the first stage of the construction of the chateau a park, in the style of French Baroque gardens, was taking shape outside the west wing under the guidance of Dutch experts. The garden casino with Lanzani’s decoration and a fountain by Peter Wiliame, has not survived and only the romantic Chinese pavilion from the 1780s remains. In the mid-19th century the garden, covering 15 hectares, was simplified in the “English” style. A reconstruction in the 1970s partially restored the Baroque appearance of the chateau parterre with pools and fountains and re-installed the mythological and allegorical stone figures.

091b9985-830d-5a24-aeb3-8b6403f919cf.name: St. Paulo Obelisk Fountain
091b9985-830d-5a24-aeb3-8b6403f919cf.description: From the Mãe d' Água das Amoreiras, a secondary aqueduct spreads out around the city terminating in fountains, many of them like this one still extant. Designed by Reinaldo Manuel dos Santos in 1774, it was not built until 1848, with minor adaptations by Malaquias Ferreira Leal.
091b9985-830d-5a24-aeb3-8b6403f919cf.artist: Design: Reinaldo Manuel dos Santos [n.d.]; adapted by Malaquias Ferreira Leal (1790–1855)

0b97dc8a-3cf2-52e7-ae54-70cec9694c3e.name: Main Altar
0b97dc8a-3cf2-52e7-ae54-70cec9694c3e.description: Two pairs of columns flank the main altar on both sides. According to the church’s patrocinium, the figures of both Johns, the Evangelist and the Baptist, are positioned beside it and are among some of Franz Xaver Schmädl’s best works. In contrast, the altarpiece depicts the Crucifixion of Christ as the beginning of the divine work of salvation. The austere design of the columns around the altar stands in strong contrast to the capriciously arranged side altars, illustrating the hierarchical order between them.
0b97dc8a-3cf2-52e7-ae54-70cec9694c3e.artist: Altar: Thassilo Zöpf (1723–1807); Altarpiece: Johann Baptist Baader (1717–80); Sculptor: Franz Xaver Schmädl (1705–77)

0e7a534f-4091-5533-9e34-fa83788eea0c.name: Chapel of the Sorrowful Mother (Fieger Chapel)
0e7a534f-4091-5533-9e34-fa83788eea0c.description: Built as an extension to the vestibule, it was donated Johann Karl Graf Fieger. Together with the magnificent column altar, the most significant feature is the ceiling frescos from Kaspar Waldmann, a glorification of Mary with the seven founders of the Servite Order and scenes from the life of Mary.
0e7a534f-4091-5533-9e34-fa83788eea0c.location: Northern vestibule, The Servite Monastery Church of St. Charles Borromeo

14cf3ac9-f201-5ffe-96c6-9da83f2f8352.name: Library Façade
14cf3ac9-f201-5ffe-96c6-9da83f2f8352.description: Magnificent Baroque façade in limestone with four huge columns crowned by the royal coat of arms and the phrase “So highly are books praised here in Coimbra that a library crowns the city head”.

15a87fb6-8298-5ff6-a114-ee8cde8ea202.name: Pulpit
15a87fb6-8298-5ff6-a114-ee8cde8ea202.description: A beautiful example of an Early Classicist pulpit in austere forms virtually without ornamentation or pictorial programme. Instead of Baroque rhetoric—which was no longer expected of the preacher—the pulpit was designed to provide a dignified frame for an edifying sermon. The design originates from Hagenauer and Nesselthaler and was executed by Peter Pflauder, a stucco mason and altar carpenter from Thannheim in Tyrol.

17c6b768-948a-514c-ad9b-2dc3c8992cd0.name: Side altars
17c6b768-948a-514c-ad9b-2dc3c8992cd0.description: Six virtuosically carved altars mounted in the niches flanking the chancel arch depicting patrons (from left to right: St. Catherine, St. Corbinian, Holy Apostles, Holy Family, St. Benedict, St. Sebastian) as well as the pulpit, are regarded as masterpieces of Johann Baptist Straub. The altarpieces, flanked by sculptures, were made among others by Martin Knoller and Johann Jakob Zeiller.
17c6b768-948a-514c-ad9b-2dc3c8992cd0.artist: Johann Baptist Straub (1704–1784); Johann Jakob Zeiller (1710–1783); Martin Knoller (1725–1804)

1a5ad99e-4e60-596e-9113-8c0b78eebfe2.name: Large reading tables
1a5ad99e-4e60-596e-9113-8c0b78eebfe2.description: The six large tables (buffets) in multi-coloured and exotic woods are all slightly different and designed to match each room.
1a5ad99e-4e60-596e-9113-8c0b78eebfe2.location: Interior, Biblioteca Joanina da Universidade de Coimbra

1b3c9fc4-faee-59ed-b3c7-369b7488c0f3.name: Library
1b3c9fc4-faee-59ed-b3c7-369b7488c0f3.description: Above the sacristy and the Chapel of St. Anne is one of a few surviving monastery libraries. The vault features scenes from the life of St. Norbert connected with the celebration of the Eucharist. The painting’s concept, flying in the face of common iconography, was probably by the monastery abbot. The relief decorations of the library cases are symbols of the sciences and arts. A large quantity of the books came from dissolved monasteries in the surrounding area, especially Louka u Znojma; one section was assembled by the abbot of the Cistercian Monastery in Düsselthal in the Rhine basin, which was purchased by the monastery in 1802.

254423af-fde7-552f-b490-c82fbb4023ad.name: High altar
254423af-fde7-552f-b490-c82fbb4023ad.description: The high altar, designed by Schnegg, with its prospect of dark-red marbled pillars, forms the focal point of the enfilade. The altar painting of the highest quality is probably the work of Maulpertsch who painted the Riesensaal in Innsbruck at about this time. The brilliantly polished white sculptures, which stand out from the church’s brightly coloured interior, depict, amongst others, the patrons of the diocese of Brixen. The monumental, but nonetheless elegant figures are of striking quality.

267869f3-46a7-515e-bdba-038ab6a15510.name: *Glory of the Benedictine Order*
267869f3-46a7-515e-bdba-038ab6a15510.description: The large dome fresco glorifies, approved by the Holy Trinity, the mission of the Benedictine Order in terms of God’s plan for salvation and includes several hundred figures.

2a8f2ad2-0175-5d0b-b8ba-1b55369ff2d5.name: Façade
2a8f2ad2-0175-5d0b-b8ba-1b55369ff2d5.description: The façade, with its two lightly projecting towers framing the two-storey central section structured in three vertical axes with tail gable, is a later successor to Salzburg Cathedral. However, they are quite different in character – the Early Baroque model appears considerably bulkier and more austere, the Early Classicist successor more two-dimensional and with finer proportions and structure.

31a2ed6c-a768-5550-a180-6fecff19b3b0.name: Exterior, south façade
31a2ed6c-a768-5550-a180-6fecff19b3b0.description: Designed by Gumpp in 1754, the Hofgasse Wing was completed according to his plans by 1756. The centre of the wing is composed of a monumental portal projection in the form of a gabled triumphal arch encompassing all four storeys. It is only here that Johann Martin Gumpp’s façade conception has been realised completely in accordance with his ideas. The influence of his brother Georg Anton’s country house façade is evident. The ponderous Late Baroque style has been adjusted to contemporary taste with the addition of rocaille work on the windows.

31a85a61-1ef8-530b-8b89-bfb3cb6f169d.name: Memorial Chapel for Emperor Franz I
31a85a61-1ef8-530b-8b89-bfb3cb6f169d.description: On the order of Maria Theresa the room in which the emperor died in August 1765 was converted into a memorial chapel by Pacassi and an endowment for ladies of rank was founded in his honour. The hall, structured with pilasters, is adorned with gentle rocaille stucco of which the tribune features a painted relief group of God the Father with mourning angels from Franz Anton Leitensdorffer (1721–95).

37077acc-2bd2-556b-ada4-0cdd3f56fffb.name: Rua das Amoreiras Arch
37077acc-2bd2-556b-ada4-0cdd3f56fffb.description: Thanks to the architectural risk-taking of Carlos Mardel, the Rua das Amoreiras arch was built between 1746 and 1748. Two things make this monumental structure particularly notable: its innovation, for over the final perpendicular branch of the aqueduct the water galleries from Alcântara run and this had never before been seen; and the engineering – from here the aqueduct turns sharp right to the Mãe d'Água reservoir. The Amoreiras Arch frames the Rua das Amoreiras and represented at one time an “entrance”, as if it were an arch in a defensive wall, highlighting both the exceptional status of this hydraulic masterpiece and its setting.

3833a71f-0ae4-54fa-a584-49250b36be5a.name: High Altar of St. Catherine of Alexandria
3833a71f-0ae4-54fa-a584-49250b36be5a.description: The illusionist fresco St. Catherine Among Alexandrine philosophers and Writers is a quality *trompe l'oeil* painting displaying illusionist architecture of the Alexandrian temple with the huge figures of St. Catherine and her collocutors occupying the central part of the composition. The painted space spreads towards the background in almost accurate central perspective. On the sides, just above eye level, are St. Paul on the left and St. Peter on the right, while the attic is dedicated to the Holy Trinity accompanied by angels.
3833a71f-0ae4-54fa-a584-49250b36be5a.location: The sanctuary, eastern wall, Academy Church of St. Catherine

3d279afa-014f-54de-b5b3-c820b9b5e080.name: Grand Hall
3d279afa-014f-54de-b5b3-c820b9b5e080.description: The most significant and artistically most important room in the building is the Grand Hall on the second floor, designed after the fire of 1785. Stucco decorations on the walls imitate grey marble with dark veins, while at one time those of the vault were painted light yellow. Architectural decoration powerfully articulates the surfaces.
3d279afa-014f-54de-b5b3-c820b9b5e080.location: Second floor, Palace of the Sugar Refinery

451de532-a903-5a8c-9c94-39a46adafd1f.name: *Presentation of the Miraculous Picture*
451de532-a903-5a8c-9c94-39a46adafd1f.description: The fresco depicts the Abbey’s foundation legend, as in Pisa the donor Emperor Ludwig (Louis) the Bavarian receives the miraculous picture from an angelic-looking monk.

4538f38d-a64f-5f64-ba07-d2b5bab3e669.name: Riesensaal
4538f38d-a64f-5f64-ba07-d2b5bab3e669.description: The “Riesensaal”, whose name is derived from an earlier cycle of Hercules paintings, together with the court chapel, is the second room dedicated to the memory of Emperor Franz I and designed according to the model of the Grand Gallery in Schönbrunn Palace. The banqueting hall extending across the whole width of the wing on Rennweg encompasses two storeys and seven window axes. It is furnished in honour of the House of Habsburg. The huge fresco panels depict allegories, the oil paintings the family of the imperial couple.

4fe53e71-5945-5d6a-9e28-e7a34d244285.name: Freemasons’ Room
4fe53e71-5945-5d6a-9e28-e7a34d244285.description: The decoration of the chateau was completed in the early 19th century, in the spirit of the “spiritual alchemy” of the late Enlightenment. The Mniszeks finished the Empire-style construction of the stable frontage and made minor Neo-Gothic and Romantic adjustments to the frontages. They also built chapels, crosses, obelisks and family memorials in the park. In 1816 Stanislav Mniszek purchased a stoneware factory and turned it into a famous manufactory.

5356a6b6-e734-542a-9ab6-73a3c0d9aadd.name: The Life of St. John the Baptist
5356a6b6-e734-542a-9ab6-73a3c0d9aadd.description: Johann Baptist Baader’s ceiling fresco spans an area of over 160 square meters above the nave. A natural landscape in the foreground and an architectural backdrop impressively envelope the depictions of the life of St. John the Baptist, providing structure for their arrangement at the same time. In the spirit of enlightenment, allegories are omitted here in favour of historical topics. From the design of the powerful trompe l’oeil architecture, Baader was clearly inspired by the style of Andrea Pozzo’s dome frescoes, which his Augsburgian teacher Johann Georg Bergmüller conveyed to him. Moreover, some of the staffage figures illustrate how Baader was greatly influenced by Neapolitan ceiling frescoes during a sojourn in Italy lasting several years.

5b66ccc1-4f4e-5e59-afac-9cb5613ba254.name: Staircase
5b66ccc1-4f4e-5e59-afac-9cb5613ba254.description: The Italian artists were part of the D. Martinelli circle, participating in the construction of the Liechtenstein palace in Vienna. The stucco artist, Bussi, also worked with Fischer von Erlach and J. L. Hildebrandt.

6110f5b1-3f44-5eb5-b9ee-45cff6f20302.name: Relief cycle, *Life of the Virgin Mary*
6110f5b1-3f44-5eb5-b9ee-45cff6f20302.description: Ten oval, gilded lead reliefs with pictures depicting the Life of the Virgin Mary are mounted on the marble high altar.

65e0961f-c135-53b7-936d-31d97f565267.name: Ceiling fresco: *The Veneration of St. Charles Borromeo*
65e0961f-c135-53b7-936d-31d97f565267.description: The frescos in Volders are among the most important of Knoller’s works. The apotheosis of the church patron in the main cupola is the high point of the programme, surrounded by scenes from his life. As an important representative of the Counter Reformation his veneration goes hand in hand with the victory of Catholicism. Knoller’s clear composition with monumental figures already contains elements of Classicism.
65e0961f-c135-53b7-936d-31d97f565267.location: Main cupola, The Servite Monastery Church of St. Charles Borromeo

6be16235-7200-5556-9bd2-0e18c38a6fca.name: St. Norbert
6be16235-7200-5556-9bd2-0e18c38a6fca.description: The painting of a side altar altarpiece is dedicated to the founder of the Premonstratensian order, St. Norbert, set into an illusionary painted altar with other “statues” of saints. The scene, climaxing in the Host, symbol of the Lord’s body, opens with the figure of an angel in counter-light. The light emanates from inside the picture and the viewer, deceived by the optical illusion of altar architecture, is pulled into the scene – a celestial sphere with glorified saint.

6be75fcb-c136-5464-b836-1965beae6a26.name: Façade
6be75fcb-c136-5464-b836-1965beae6a26.description: The entire idiosyncrasy and fancy of the Early Baroque building can be best seen on the façade which appears as if it was pieced together from a construction kit composed of the most bizarre forms. The departure from the classical theory of form shows that the dilettante architect (= enthusiast) was still an adherent of Mannerism, drawing his vocabulary of forms from religious tracts. Little of the often classical austerity of German Early Baroque is in evidence here. The chapels at the sides of the façade were added later in accordance with the existing design.

71e649d1-8512-5c78-b45e-dbe9c62e5ac6.name: Ceiling fresco: *Glorification of Mary*
71e649d1-8512-5c78-b45e-dbe9c62e5ac6.description: The choir fresco depicts a pristine Heaven of the Saints devoid of architectural set pieces or landscapes. The composition of the venerated Mary in the midst of the Fourteen Holy Helpers consists of groups of figures arranged on the clouds like spectators on the tiers of a theatre, as opposed to tracing a circular form. Here we have left the earthly sphere of the two western frescos and the glory of heaven is expressed in bright, airy colours.

724ecf67-8522-5e73-9afd-9978350e2c01.name: Hall of the Ancestors
724ecf67-8522-5e73-9afd-9978350e2c01.description:
Chancellor Václav Antonín completed reconstruction of a former garden room with a ceiling painting of the Gods on Mount Olympus and displayed larger-than-life portraits of his parents, grandparents and his wife.  
The Hall of the Ancestors is connected to the oval Historical Hall by illusionary painted architecture. It was here that the truce between Austria and France was signed after the Battle of Austerlitz.

767b259b-ec09-5677-98c7-f929983f4b2b.name: Drawing of  Pombaline Façades
767b259b-ec09-5677-98c7-f929983f4b2b.description:
Fire became a major concern after the earthquake of 1755 when tightly packed downtown Lisbon was consumed by fire that swept through the narrow streets and quickly destroyed buildings that were built closely together.  
Henceforth, buildings were separated by stone walls in order to isolate them. The uniform, multi-storey Pombaline façades (with shops, three domestic floors and an attic) are unique, constructed at a time when the focus was on safety and cost was a priority.  
The uniformity of the façades and windows is linked to the cost controls that dictated reconstruction: installation of the doors and windows were straightforward once all the stone frames had been made with identical measurements. The addition of a coat of arms was not allowed.

792acd8a-ec3d-58f9-aac4-9e904aebd7b3.name: Altar of St. Ignatius
792acd8a-ec3d-58f9-aac4-9e904aebd7b3.description: Archbishop Emerik Esterhazy was the donor for the marble Altar of St. Ignatius. In its architectural structure, the altarpiece belongs to a type designed for jesuit churches by Andrea Pozzo. The two side sculptures represent the two Jesuit saints, St. Frances Regis and St. Frances Xavier.
792acd8a-ec3d-58f9-aac4-9e904aebd7b3.location: The first side chapel of St. Ignatius on the left-hand (north) side of the nave

79ee1d89-b25b-54b7-9f77-22260ee5d520.name: Vault of the Grand Hall
79ee1d89-b25b-54b7-9f77-22260ee5d520.description: The vault is divided into four sections by diagonal strips. In between each section, there are round medallions with scenes from Roman military history, as well as emblems with the motifs of antique military equipment: shields, torches and flags.
79ee1d89-b25b-54b7-9f77-22260ee5d520.location: Second floor, Palace of the Sugar Refinery

83a35999-406e-5ef3-a9b6-1e038d1d60e2.name: Three out of the six original plans with a new layout sympathetic to the old one; final plan and orthophoto of Lisbon
83a35999-406e-5ef3-a9b6-1e038d1d60e2.description: Following the earthquake of 1755, the Marquis of Pombal rapidly ordered a competition for the design of *Baixa Pombalina*. Six plans were submitted from which he would select the winner. On 4 December 1755, Manuel da Maia and Eugénio dos Santos presented plans that proposed replacing Terreiro do Paço (Palace Square) with Praça do Comércio, conceived as a monumental entrance into the town through the Cais das Colunas (Columns Quay).
83a35999-406e-5ef3-a9b6-1e038d1d60e2.artist: Military engineers: Manuel da Maia (1677–1766), Eugénio dos Santos (1711–1760)

84149fe6-4a0e-5c7e-942e-8173633f866e.name: *Gaiolas* Building Structure
84149fe6-4a0e-5c7e-942e-8173633f866e.description: *The Gaiola Pombalina* is a remarkable symmetrical structure built from wood to distribute and balance the forces of an earthquake. All buildings in downtown Lisbon were built according to this system, and this is the world's first anti-seismic structure. This prototype, built by the fire department at the beginning of the 20th century, is used for fire-fighting training.
84149fe6-4a0e-5c7e-942e-8173633f866e.location: *Baixa Pombalina* or downtown Lisbon. These drawings are displayed in Museu da Cidade and a prototype is in the Museu dos Bombeiros.
84149fe6-4a0e-5c7e-942e-8173633f866e.artist: Eugénio dos Santos (1711–1760); Carlos Mardel (c. 1695–1763), Manuel da Maia (1677–1766)

8c6e7a5a-f8b4-50cb-b4d1-b5bba30ca387.name: Dominik Ondřej Kounic with the Order of the Golden Fleece
8c6e7a5a-f8b4-50cb-b4d1-b5bba30ca387.description: The spur for the spectacular reconstruction of a Renaissance palace for the Kounic family came from Dominik Ondřej of Kounice, Imperial Vice-Chancellor. Kounic first commissioned the Bavarian architect Zuccali and later D. Martinelli, who had worked for the family in other parts of the demesne (Uherský Brod). Only the west wing was completed. The bust was created by Jan Blommendael, portraitist of William III Oranje-Nassau (Mauritshuis). Kounic stayed in the Hague during the peace negotiations that took place between 1695 and1697. He was also portrayed by Hyacinth Rigaud.

8e48c406-81de-53cf-94cd-3dd8775f331d.name: Pulpit
8e48c406-81de-53cf-94cd-3dd8775f331d.description: The pulpit, with its wooden core freely ornamented with stucco is one of the most remarkable Rococo pulpits in the entire south German-speaking region. An exemplary feature is the towering baldachin with its rocaille work ascending freely like waves, a masterpiece of the stucco mason’s art. The rocaille work of the baldachin contains symbols of the sermon – Tablets of the Law, flaming sword and the holy spirit in the form of a dove – while the pulpit itself has a purely ornamental design.
8e48c406-81de-53cf-94cd-3dd8775f331d.location: East side of the nave, central pillar

914274d1-3d96-57be-befe-0bf0a94e33ac.name: *Vojslava of Hrádek*
914274d1-3d96-57be-befe-0bf0a94e33ac.description: Legend has it that the monastery was founded in 1211 by Markvard of Hrádek and his wife Vojslava. Their fictitious portraits originally decorated the refectory. The couple is represented in 17th-century attire. Their spiritual intentions made clear by their gestures, their majestic posture illustrates their determination in the execution of theose intentions. The composition, a richly ornamented table and background covered in drapery, is a traditional painting scheme.

9767c365-8093-52c3-83c1-3946d0072faa.name: View from the east
9767c365-8093-52c3-83c1-3946d0072faa.description: Although the arrangement of the rest of the building is not as closely crowded as the façade, the walls are still un-classical in their configuration. The superstructure with perimeter pilasters throughout and an attic zone is modelled on St. Peter’s in Rome, as is the building’s basic design with domed tri-conch. The tower, expressing the motif of the Trinity, was originally designed with a spiral-shaped pinnacle.

9779dbd4-5cc7-5f2e-8017-625b454897d3.name: High altar
9779dbd4-5cc7-5f2e-8017-625b454897d3.description: The powerful, Early Baroque high altar, which was reworked in the 18th century, is one of the earliest two-leveled conceptions in Bavaria serving a pilgrimage cult. Statues of the bishopric patron, St. Ulrich, and the order’s patron, St. Augustine, stand between pillars. A fold-away altarpiece painting referring to the legend of the pilgrimage once stood at the centre of the altar, behind this would have been an upper altar that was reserved for a spiritual dignitary. The miraculous, legendarily supposed Thassilo-Crucifix which replaced the painting in reality dates from about 1230. The front of the crucifix shows an image of Christ crucified covered with horse skin. This originally would have been placed near to the pilgrims on the lower altar. In the 18th century, Johann Baptist Straub used the space vacated by the crucifix for a marvelous tabernacle with figures of the Holy Emperor Heinrich and his wife Kunigunde as well as allegories of Faith, Hope and Love. Sensitively rendered reliefs appear typologically on the sacrifice of the mass: the Harvest of Manna, the Last Supper and Supper at Emmaus.
9779dbd4-5cc7-5f2e-8017-625b454897d3.artist: Hans Krumpper (1570–1634); Benedikt Meggas; Bartholomäus Steinle (1580–1628/29); Johann Baptist Straub (1704–1784)

9c12405d-2e2a-59f6-85f0-cd79f698c73d.name: Chapel of St. Anne
9c12405d-2e2a-59f6-85f0-cd79f698c73d.description: The chapel protrudes from the otherwise smooth façade of the east wing of the monastery, adjoining the sacristy. In 1639 a crypt was built there to contain the tomb of Provost Plocar who commissioned the construction of the monastery. The chapel vaults and walls are covered with illusionary painting. The coats of arms are associated with the “mother” monastery in Brno-Zábrdovice. The richly carved retable from 1702, holding an image of God the Father, frames a Gothic statue of St. Anne.

9d1b3ddb-6a64-5dc1-ae7b-afa6d1da6b9b.name: Exterior, east façade
9d1b3ddb-6a64-5dc1-ae7b-afa6d1da6b9b.description: The Hofburg’s main façade differs significantly from that facing the Hofgasse. The wing was erected between 1766–80 according to plans from Pacassi and under the direction of the Viennese military architect Constantin Walter von Pfeilsberg. Gumpp’s plan was abandoned in favour of a new conception. The elongated, lightly curved front is designed along the lines of the Viennese palace built at the same time. It has a high basement storey and colossal order, with two seven-axis portal projections and rounded corner pavilions composed of existing towers.

9d1f5f8c-ef4a-5842-b57a-0d05acb3531b.name: Ceiling frescos: *St Gall during the building of the monastery*
9d1f5f8c-ef4a-5842-b57a-0d05acb3531b.description: The sequence of ceiling pictures – three illusionistic cupolas and corresponding spandrel pictures – begin with the story of the church patron Gall executed in subdued colours which become increasingly brighter in the two subsequent cupola frescos. The saint, situated in a landscape scene, is depicted as the abbot (which he never actually was) of the monastery of St. Gallen under construction. The presentation of the building plan effectively represents the act of founding. The cupola fresco, partly situated above the organ loft, is designed to be viewed facing west.

9dddcf81-e7ef-57de-826f-00c891445be3.name: Imaginary cityscape in the Salon with Panoramic Views
9dddcf81-e7ef-57de-826f-00c891445be3.description: The wall paintings of imaginary cityscapes reveal the influence of the architectural drawings of Giovanni Battista Piranesi.
9dddcf81-e7ef-57de-826f-00c891445be3.location: Second floor, west salon, Palace of the Sugar Refinery

aaa73ab6-82bc-549b-89fe-7ef1622228fa.name: Altar of St. Dionisius (Altar of the Holy Martyrs)
aaa73ab6-82bc-549b-89fe-7ef1622228fa.description: The Altar of St. Dionisius combines sculptures by the early Baroque sculptor from Varasdin, Ivan Jakob Altenbach, and paintings by the Slovenina painter, Hans Georg Geiger. The first domestic sculptor of major artistic note, Ivan Jakob Altenbach appeared in the mid-1670s. His work shows essentially that he overcame the surviving forms of Mannerism to achieve the stylistic features of the Baroque. The Jesuit church in Leoben, Styria, influenced the conservative, two-storey structure of the wooden retable.
aaa73ab6-82bc-549b-89fe-7ef1622228fa.location: The side chapel of St. Martyrs (St. Dionisius) on the right-hand (south) side of the nave
aaa73ab6-82bc-549b-89fe-7ef1622228fa.artist: Ivan Jakob Altenbach (active c. 1675–d. before 1692), Hans Georg Geiger (active 1639–d. 1681)

aad909a1-b106-56bf-86ee-b7aee4a41eef.name: Central ceiling fresco in the Riesensaal
aad909a1-b106-56bf-86ee-b7aee4a41eef.description: The painted ceiling, including the painted stucco, covers an area of c. 500 square metres and is one of Franz Anton Maulbertsch’s major works. The empress personally contributed to its design. The central fresco shows an allegory of the union of the royal houses of Austria and Lorraine, the flanking ovals depict the regalia of Tyrol. The marriage of the houses of Austria and Lorraine is depicted as a chariot, accompanied by personifications of the sovereign’s virtues.

ab501a21-ec14-5a97-af8f-4cbadd1c1cc2.name: The Altar of St. Agatha
ab501a21-ec14-5a97-af8f-4cbadd1c1cc2.description: The side altar made of stucco marble is dedicated to St. Agatha, a patron of farmers. Instead of a painting, an alcove holds Schmädl’s sculpture of the martyr. The scroll-shaped volutes to the sides lend the altar an extremely ornamental character. Symbolic of the opening of Heaven, a golden circlet sits above the altar behind which an obelisk crowned with a vase towers as a Christian symbol of victory.
ab501a21-ec14-5a97-af8f-4cbadd1c1cc2.artist: Altar: Thassilo Zöpf (1723–1807); Sculptor: Franz Xaver Schmädl (1705–77)

add54831-b132-5b1c-9ed1-5c4eec59a759.name: Praça do Comércio
add54831-b132-5b1c-9ed1-5c4eec59a759.description: Praça do Comércio overlooking the River Tejo is an emblematic part of the *Baixa*. According to the engraving attributed to Gaspar Froes Machado, the initial plans were not entirely fulfilled; the triumphal arch was finally built in 1873 according to the design of Veríssimo José da Costa.
add54831-b132-5b1c-9ed1-5c4eec59a759.location: Facing the estuary of the River Tagus
add54831-b132-5b1c-9ed1-5c4eec59a759.artist: Initial plans of Praça do Comércio: Manuel da Maia (1677–1766), Eugénio dos Santos (1711–1760); Carlos Mardel (c. 1695–1763); triumphal arch: Veríssimo José da Costa [n.d.] assisted by Vítor Bastos (1830–1894) and Anatole C. Calmels (1822–1906)

b4d6753b-ee3a-5120-a57e-e35af32589c1.name: Hall of the Ancestors
b4d6753b-ee3a-5120-a57e-e35af32589c1.description: The monumental and technically demanding building on an unusual elliptical ground plan, celebrates a Swabian-Bavarian dynasty that settled in Moravia in the second half of the 16th century. Statues in the niches represent real and mythical family figures. Erlach followed in the footsteps of Bernini in the design. The memorial building changed function in the mid-18th century when the Hall, with its pre-Romanticism terraces, became a viewing point for surveying the beautiful countryside around the chateau.
b4d6753b-ee3a-5120-a57e-e35af32589c1.artist: Johann Bernhard Fischer von Erlach (1656 Graz – 1723 Vienna), Tobias Kracker (1658–1736, Vienna)

b669842e-6ceb-5465-9eca-126b151afac3.name: *Assumption and Heavenly Reception of the Virgin Mary*
b669842e-6ceb-5465-9eca-126b151afac3.description: The complex Neoclassical dome fresco depicts Christ’s reception of the Virgin Mary in heaven together with biblical figures. It is clearly related to the high altarpiece depicting the *Assumption of the Virgin Mary*.
b669842e-6ceb-5465-9eca-126b151afac3.location: High altar and dome of the chancel

bbf2ac31-f420-5547-903d-485e39009fa1.name: Arches over the Alcântara valley
bbf2ac31-f420-5547-903d-485e39009fa1.description: The structure uses the pointed arch in some of the larger arches crossing the Alcântara valley. Curiously, some of the stones of the Aqueduct are inscribed with the masons' initials, a custom that was all but lost but which was revived here.

bfde98ff-c1bf-5790-801d-18b84b741f38.name: Ceiling frescos: *Care of the Arts* – *Theological Truth* – *Profane Truth*
bfde98ff-c1bf-5790-801d-18b84b741f38.description: The central ceiling image of the library hall displays Theological Truth through Divine Revelation. In the next fresco, Parnassus as the Mountain of the Muses with feminine allegories shows the close relationship between the arts, and likewise, the close relationship between the monastery and the modern sciences. On the other side Truth, in the sense of profane critical science, is taken as a theme illustrating the “unveiling of truth”, which at the same time underlines the quintessence of the entire programme. The depiction is based on the title page of Diderot's *Encyclopédie*, the famous encyclopedia of the Enlightenment, which was perceived at the time to bring together the entirety of knowledge from the sciences, the arts and the trades. Provost Fanciscus Töpsl leaves behind his intellectual legacy by using his coat-of-arms: he sees himself not only as the third founder and decisive reformer of his foundation, but likewise, as father of its enlightened mission to instruct and inform.
bfde98ff-c1bf-5790-801d-18b84b741f38.location: Vault of the Library Hall, Augustinian Canons’ Convent of the Holy Saviour

c18e8d6d-69e1-5154-b742-7142e553dfce.name: Stuccowork
c18e8d6d-69e1-5154-b742-7142e553dfce.description: Stucco floral ornamentation and figurative scenes depict the life of the patron saint and saints to which the side chapels were dedicated between 1713 and 1726. The stuccowork, by the Italian master Anton Joseph Quadrio, was constructed between 1713 and 1721, and an anonymous Italian master between 1724 and 1726. With this exquisite work, St. Catherine's reached the ideal of *bel composto*, the characteristic Baroque unity of architecture, sculpture and painting.

c256056a-455e-5666-97c9-214e4f117e0d.name: Ceiling painting: *Competition of the Magician Simon with Peter and Paul*
c256056a-455e-5666-97c9-214e4f117e0d.description: Victory over evil and unbelief, which frequently commences the programme of pictures, is here drawn from the story of the two church patrons: The apostles demonstrate the truth of the Christian faith in front of the entire people, evil in the form of the magician is destroyed. In a spatial image made up of a range of perspectives, different levels are combined with virtuosity to form an overall impression: Late Baroque pictorial rhetoric employing clear colours and audacious composition.

c27eb774-cc9f-55db-b3e3-343e34b005f2.name: Middle room balcony railings
c27eb774-cc9f-55db-b3e3-343e34b005f2.description: Each room has a different colour scheme and decorative emphasis with multicoloured bookshelves of different lacquered finishes in green, red and black decorated with *chinoiserie* motifs. Each of the rooms is two-storeys high, with a balcony and stairs incorporated into the furniture.
c27eb774-cc9f-55db-b3e3-343e34b005f2.location: Interior, Biblioteca Joanina da Universidade de Coimbra
c27eb774-cc9f-55db-b3e3-343e34b005f2.artist: Design and execution: Francesco Gualdini, João Rodrigues de Almeida; supervisor: Gaspar Ferreira; painting and gilding of woodwork: Manuel da Silva [dates unknown]

c6cb3e56-81b8-5635-ab45-fa274e89c1c4.name: Ceiling fresco
c6cb3e56-81b8-5635-ab45-fa274e89c1c4.description: Following his apprenticeship, Schöpf, a student of Knoller, is considered one of the most important masters of fresco painting during the transition to Early Classicism. The composition of the large cupola fresco depicting the Coronation of the Virgin Mary follows the Late Baroque scheme with a crown of clouds and vision of light in the centre, however the painting style, above all in the case of the figures, is characterised by concentration and devout earnestness. Baroque pathos is replaced by a salutary pictorial narrative.

c9e437ac-0abc-54f8-bdb1-c612628c79a0.name: Celebration of the Althann Dynasty
c9e437ac-0abc-54f8-bdb1-c612628c79a0.description: Illusionary elements of a balustrade and carpet provide a link between the earth and the celestial sphere. Ancient gods and allegorical figures show a path to honour and glory. The family’s celestial triumph is accompanied by scenes depicting aristocratic virtues. The major component is not stuccowork but painting, in contrast to more recent decorations. The fresco as one of the first pieces by an artist who later became famous.

cc3d0593-4799-50e0-9f3d-44bc2af39e0e.name: Staircase
cc3d0593-4799-50e0-9f3d-44bc2af39e0e.description: The Imperial-style staircase has three flights. It bears characteristics typical of the 1780s, consisting of superimposed columns, strips and cornices originally painted in a marble paint finish, while the railing has a decorative motif of a square meander, which also points to the Early Classical language of architecture.
cc3d0593-4799-50e0-9f3d-44bc2af39e0e.location: Central area (opposite the entrance hall), Palace of the Sugar Refinery

ce8830d8-b822-5a73-b84f-3d1865e4c511.name: Workshops and houses for craftsmen
ce8830d8-b822-5a73-b84f-3d1865e4c511.description: The narrow streets of the hamlet with houses on both sides remind the urban structure of the medieval town of Bologna.

cfe4e76b-dae8-5b07-88b5-6d61d4cac871.name: Relic chapel
cfe4e76b-dae8-5b07-88b5-6d61d4cac871.description: What is commonly known as the *Achbergkapelle* (Relic Chapel), so-called due to a miraculous sculptured image of the Virgin Mary, contains a splendid stucco marble altar wall with integrated relic shrines and atmospheric Neapolitan-influenced oil paintings on the ceiling depicting the Life of Christ.
cfe4e76b-dae8-5b07-88b5-6d61d4cac871.location: Ground floor of the choir, to the right of the presbytery, Augustinian Canons’ Convent of the Holy Saviour

d2984278-366b-5283-9f1a-506cabf83a53.name: Façade and tower
d2984278-366b-5283-9f1a-506cabf83a53.description: Together with the west tower, the façade forms a delightful ensemble, a simplified version of the double-tower façade of Wilten parish church (since 1964 St. Jacob’s Cathedral). The few sculptural architectural elements – mouldings, tail gable and portal aedicule – are supplemented by painting and sculpture. The gable panel features an *Ecclesia triumphans*, painted by Günther, together with the church patrons in the niches of the façade wall from Schnegg (the triumphant Catholic Church, founded by Peter and Paul).
d2984278-366b-5283-9f1a-506cabf83a53.artist: Franz Singer (1724–1789); Johann Schnegg (1724–1784); Matthäus Günther (1705–1788)

d2a0bb6d-e271-5430-bd69-fba3a45eaf85.name:
Bronze Equestrian Statue of King José I  
(copper engraving by Carneiro da Silva made before the unveiling in 1774)
d2a0bb6d-e271-5430-bd69-fba3a45eaf85.description: The statue by Joaquim Machado de Castro was unveiled on 27 May 1775 on King José I’s birthday. The copper engraving by Joaquim Carneiro da Silva was made a year prior to this in 1774 to commemorate the unveiling. Other commemorative items include china decorated with reproductions of the statue.
d2a0bb6d-e271-5430-bd69-fba3a45eaf85.location: Terreiro do Paço (Palace Square) or Praça do Comércio (Commerce  Square)

d6106d67-8053-5953-b8d3-21dcd5e36a0d.name: Mãe d’ Água das Amoreiras reservoir
d6106d67-8053-5953-b8d3-21dcd5e36a0d.description: Mãe d' Água das Amoreiras reservoir was designed by Carlos Mardel. Due to its monumentality, the Mãe d'Água constitutes a true civic temple to the *águas livres* (free waters). An antechamber precedes the vast rectangle which contains a deep reservoir.

d8289a89-1170-5ec0-a741-c5175017f870.name: Chapel of the Holy Trinity
d8289a89-1170-5ec0-a741-c5175017f870.description: This chateau chapel, with a subterranean family tomb, is a conceptual and compositional counterpart to the Hall of the Ancestors. The cylindrical central nave, with six oval apses around the perimeter, is decorated with paintings – the Last Judgment, Heaven and Paradise – drawing attention to the ephemeral nature of existence, the end of human life and its continuation in eternity. The cupola fresco represents the Archangel Michael, the family’s patron saint and protector of the Church.
d8289a89-1170-5ec0-a741-c5175017f870.artist: Johann Bernhard Fischer von Erlach (1656 Graz – 1723 Vienna), Ignaz Heinitz of Heintzenthal (1657–1742, Vienna)

dbaffd3f-8c80-55c5-8dff-c3db51a61236.name: Courtyard
dbaffd3f-8c80-55c5-8dff-c3db51a61236.description: Countess Marie Anna Pignatelli took up the reconstruction of the residence after 1722. She commissioned the court architect A. E. Martinelli to build a three-wing chateau, adjust the entrance bridge, parts of the castle front, and the chapel frontage and interior. The two-shouldered staircase of the ceremonial courtyard is set with sculptures of Hercules fighting Antaios and Aeneas Rescuing his Father, Anchises, from Burning Troy.

dd9d98d4-ce14-5cb3-81aa-86c331412c4e.name: Altar of St. Frances Borgia
dd9d98d4-ce14-5cb3-81aa-86c331412c4e.description: The Altar of St. Francis Borgia is characterised by its conservative, two-storey architectural structure with symmetrically deployed statues. The caryatids of the bottom, the spiral columns, and the acanthus ornaments – which were actually first brought by Komersteiner to Zagreb and northern Croatia in the 1680s – introduce Baroque accents into the church. On the Altar of St. Franics Borgia, softly rounded acanthus leaves sparsely furnish the load-bearing areas and mouldings, more abundantly on the narrow wings. The design of the altarpiece is attributed to H. A. Weissenkircher.
dd9d98d4-ce14-5cb3-81aa-86c331412c4e.location: The first side chapel of St. Frances Borgia on the right-hand (south) side of the nave

e617b4a6-da47-5007-89ac-f0ffc254183c.name: High altar
e617b4a6-da47-5007-89ac-f0ffc254183c.description: The richly structured ciborium above six pillars with curved entablature and altar crown, together with the portals for the offertory procession, extend across the whole width of the choir. Its structure is clearly drawn from the high altar in Götzens. Zeiller’s altarpiece depicts the church patron Gall worshipping Mary and the Infant Jesus. The statues of six saints which flank it and the figures in the altar crown, God the Father with aureole between angels, are masterful works of an unknown sculptor.

e776e04a-2c10-552c-8dee-90065c1de43f.name: Villa Ghisilieri
e776e04a-2c10-552c-8dee-90065c1de43f.description: The villa was not only a place for leisure but also the administrative centre of many commercial and rural activities. The villa of the patron had its own courtyard, separated from the hamlet. This is where a weekly market took place.

ea9fdd0d-171f-533d-b39d-9aff5b4b8568.name: Pulpit
ea9fdd0d-171f-533d-b39d-9aff5b4b8568.description: The baptismal font, organ and particularly the pulpit, are remarkable carved pieces. Contrary to common practice they are not made of stone or stucco, and the pulpit is situated on the right decorated with plant garlands and tendrils with pomegranates. The ambo with semi-relief herm has the figures of the four Evangelists in its niches.

eb7a0351-f4ca-5902-b8bb-572d211a56e6.name: Carmo Fountain
eb7a0351-f4ca-5902-b8bb-572d211a56e6.description: From the Mãe d' Água das Amoreiras reservoir, a secondary aqueduct spreads out around the city terminating in fountains, many of them like this one still extant. Built by the engineer, Miguel Ângelo Blasco in 1769, it was redesigned by Reinaldo Manuel dos Santos in 1786.
eb7a0351-f4ca-5902-b8bb-572d211a56e6.artist: Attributed to the engineer, Miguel Ângelo Blasco (1769–1770) and the architect, Reinaldo Manuel dos Santos [n.d.]

f5088f41-3c02-57b5-88f0-03125f08fe8f.name: Ceiling fresco: *St. Gall heals a demoniac*
f5088f41-3c02-57b5-88f0-03125f08fe8f.description: The eastern nave fresco is designed in the tradition of Andrea Pozzo (1642–1709), however the cupola’s monumental illusionistic architecture is not closed, instead it opens up to reveal a view of a whole series of vaulted rooms. The grand, highly monumental architectural backdrop elevates the scene from the legend of Gall healing a demoniac to that of the triumph of the church and the history of salvation.

f7450b1c-6382-5c9c-a528-e4c11c55aa74.name: Ideal design for the residence
f7450b1c-6382-5c9c-a528-e4c11c55aa74.description: Martinelli’s design for reconstruction included the development of a major part of the town and a new parish church. The chateau, on a U-shaped ground plan with a ceremonial courtyard, reflected the status of the investor who thus laid the foundations for the future ambitions of the dynasty. The building director, Petruzzi, adjusted the design to local conditions, paying attention in particular to new functions and taste in accordance with a design by I. Valmaggini, later a building director in Vienna. Maxmilián Kounic, son of Dominik Ondřej and Secretary to Charles VI as well as a secret councillor, became a provincial governor and preferred a more austere design in the French style. The design included the segmentation of the garden with pools, parterres and mazes.

f97c18af-c344-543d-9c05-9aae43476c0f.name: Interior
f97c18af-c344-543d-9c05-9aae43476c0f.description: The space was planned by Hagenauer as a longitudinal building with a uniform sequence of four dome bays. Hueber reduced this to three, the central of which he configured as the main space above a quadratic ground plan with bevelled corner piers. Layers of pilasters and bold projecting cornices are further echoes of the Late Baroque. A sharp contrast is established by the ceiling stucco from Peter Plauder in true Early Classicist style executed in a highly two-dimensional manner, as does the austere composition of the high altar and pulpit, virtually devoid of ornamentation.
f97c18af-c344-543d-9c05-9aae43476c0f.artist: Wolfgang Hagenauer (1726–1801), Andrä Hueber [n.d.]; Peter Pflauder (1733–1811)

fb2c16ce-05ab-5038-b941-2740a8a0e2cb.name: Detail of ceiling painting
fb2c16ce-05ab-5038-b941-2740a8a0e2cb.description: The *Trompe l'oeil* ceiling painting depicts three manifestations of Wisdom: an allegory of the library (*Bibliotheca*), of the university (*Universitas*) and of the encyclopaedia (*Encyclopaedia*).
fb2c16ce-05ab-5038-b941-2740a8a0e2cb.location: Interior, Biblioteca Joanina da Universidade de Coimbra
fb2c16ce-05ab-5038-b941-2740a8a0e2cb.artist: António Simões Ribeiro and Vicente Nunes [n.d.]

fb3fdb2d-573f-563d-9108-61663265d16a.name: Portrait of João V
fb3fdb2d-573f-563d-9108-61663265d16a.description: The portrait of the King João V emerges from a sort of a “*rideau de scène*” in carved wood, upheld by angels. The oil on canvas painting is by Domenico Duprà, royal painter in Lisbon before 1730.
fb3fdb2d-573f-563d-9108-61663265d16a.location: Interior, Biblioteca Joanina da Universidade de Coimbra

fcc7b9d9-0238-5ac6-acff-da0ef5f94db3.name: High altar
fcc7b9d9-0238-5ac6-acff-da0ef5f94db3.description: The austere Classicist high altar, flanked by double columns, was executed by Pflauder according to the design of Hagenauer and Nesselthaler. In contrast, Schöpf’s masterfully executed altarpiece depicting The Assumption of Mary with its Baroque contrasts of light and shade and wealth of figures radiates calm in respect of both composition and expressive content.
fcc7b9d9-0238-5ac6-acff-da0ef5f94db3.artist: Wolfgang Hagenauer (1726–1801); Peter Pflauder (1733–1811); Joseph Schöpf (1745–1822), Andreas Nesselthaler (1748–1821)
